title: High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) Instrumentation & Modes

cognitive_progression.level_1_remember: Define fundamental laws, terminology, and bounds of High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) Instrumentation & Modes.
cognitive_progression.level_2_understand: Explain underlying physical mechanisms, instrumentation, and energy transitions.
cognitive_progression.level_3_apply: Solve quantitative analytical calculations using $$P = \frac{\eta \cdot L \cdot u}{\theta \cdot d_p^2} \quad | \quad R_s = \frac{2(t_{R2} - t_{R1})}{W_1 + W_2} \ge 1.5$$.
cognitive_progression.level_4_analyze: Interpret spectral shifts, evaluate deviations, and troubleshoot analytical anomalies.

pedagogical_boundary.retained_scope: Why high pressure is required (microparticulate packings dp = 3-5 um), HPLC components: solvent reservoirs & degassers, high pressure reciprocating pumps (isocratic vs quaternary gradient), Rheodyne injection valves, bonded stationary phases (RP-HPLC C18 Octadecylsilane and C8 vs Normal Phase silica), column ovens, detectors (UV/Vis variable wavelength, Diode Array DAD, Fluorescence, Refractive Index RID), system suitability testing (tailing factor T <= 2.0, column efficiency N > 2000, resolution Rs >= 1.5).
pedagogical_boundary.non_forced_clinical_rationale: Rigorous hardware engineering, high-pressure hydraulic pumping systems, microparticulate C18 bonded phases, and detector interfaces. Pharmacopoeial purity assays serve as analytical method benchmarks.
